The 11 new BMB/DENR CALABARZON water/habitat leads had 32 exact-name GBIF Actinopterygii searches across waterBody/locality fields (including five candidate spelling variants); all returned zero. This is a bounded discovery gap, not evidence of fish absence.

SEAFDEC 2016 Table 2 identifies a Bal-on Reservoir site and NIFEP group activities for several CALABARZON waters, but the San Pablo/Tadlak grouping is not allocated to individual lakes and six Rizal river sanctuaries are unnamed. The table gives no contemporary species survey.

SEAFDEC's 2016 proceedings reports a 7 ha Dagatan Lake in San Antonio at coordinates rounded to whole minutes and mentions Clarias macrocephalus without survey details; it does not resolve identity against Lake Pagatan or establish a dated occurrence.
Taal Lake: four exact National Museum GBIF text-field queries for Taal and Amphilophus citrinellus returned zero; this version- and field-bounded discovery result is not evidence of fish absence.

Taal Lake: two coordinate-envelope National Museum specimens match FishBase Taal catalog entries by catalog number, taxon and year, but GBIF lacks locality/waterBody and FishBase is CC BY-NC 4.0; primary catalog verification and reuse remain pending.
Taal Lake: the FishBase FW code for one GBIF/SEAFDEC catalog match conflicts with SEAOBIS institution/collection codes; verify provenance before using either candidate.

evidenceReadout.zeroResultMeaning: Exact-locality zeroes are bounded search gaps, not fish-absence findings. Waterbird monitoring and historical common-name lists are not species-level fish presence evidence.

openGaps.reason: Fourteen corrected GBIF candidates group into ten museum catalog identities. The Field Museum-hosted archive and direct CAS Ichthyology archive confirm two FMNH and six CAS SU(ICH) records with Balayan Bay locality text; the eight are admitted only as historical research-ledger evidence, with source date precision and all GBIF flags preserved. CAS publishes its selected Darwin Core archive under CC0, and the CAS 28340 source and GBIF spellings both resolve nomenclaturally to Planiliza macrolepis. The NMNH Fishes search directly confirms USNM 122919, Ventrifossa divergens and its 1908-01-20 source date; five GBIF material-citation rows therefore remain grouped under one catalog item. That record locality combines Sombrero Island, Balayan Bay and Verde Island Passage, and item-level reuse remains unresolved, so those five rows stay held. The UMMZ identity also remains unresolved. No cross-check establishes a complete or current bay checklist.
openGaps.nextAction: Resolve the six remaining held candidate rows: keep the five USNM 122919 citation rows grouped while seeking institutional guidance on the multi-locality wording and item-level reuse; continue the bounded exact-identity search for UMMZ 100346. Keep all GBIF quality flags, exclude coordinates and current-presence claims, and add no public app row until locality scope and reuse are resolved.
